review: No spinach speech comparison was identified in the retrieved results. The Japanese mixed mousse menu concerned swallowing and intake, not speech intelligibility.

Pearl millet cultivars differed on timed cognitive tasks in adolescents. A separate athletic trial found a grip-force difference and inconclusive speed/agility contrasts. Fine dexterity and Parkinson exposure remain open.
Spinach feeding studies did not measure visual hallucinations. Continue item-level Parkinson psychosis and diet data.
Probable REM sleep behavior disorder was measured in a prodromal diet cohort. Chard and dream-event frequency were not isolated.
A human rye kernel bread crossover measured cognition and mood. Continue searches for voice and acoustics in Parkinson diet interventions.
Chard search results were mainly crop, residue or broad vegetable reports. Visual hallucination data for cooked chard remain open.
Spinach chow findings differed by rod task and metric. A human spinach-extract trial registered balance and published torque; balance results were not located.

A meal study in Parkinson’s found a larger supine pressure drop but smaller orthostatic drop after eating. Barley and lightheadedness were not identified. Continue menu and orthostatic symptom records.
Buckwheat cognitive and milling reports do not supply speech intelligibility data. Continue food-symptom and meal-method searches.
Spinach animal motor learning and dietary protein studies do not test raw spinach effects on dyskinesia. Continue item and meal records.
The Parkinson-like celiac case and a mixed tremor case concern gluten withdrawal and other treatments. Neither assigns cooked wheat berries.
Thawed spinach had inconclusive attention contrasts in a healthy crossover. Preparation before commercial freezing and cooked spinach in Parkinson remain unresolved.
Rye bread crossover endpoints were cognition and mood. A separate celiac case describes improved gait after gluten withdrawal without rye attribution or freezing counts.
A sprout-powder preprint found mixed exploratory attention-task results and an inconclusive primary cognitive contrast. Mouse flour results concern maze learning.
Olfactory testing is available for a subset of a prodromal diet cohort. Continue individual cooked or steamed chard exposures.
Exact pak choi and chard records largely concerned cultivation or aroma chemistry. Pooled cruciferous results cannot identify cooked bok choy.
The millet pain search yielded grass aerial-part or leaf extracts and mismatched labor or other records. Continue oral cooked-grain pain studies.
Cooked-grain performance trials did not measure dyskinesia. Continue grain, movement and medication interaction sources.
An aged rat study measured conditioned eyeblink learning with spinach-enriched chow. The mapped clinical facial expression measure was absent.
Buckwheat preparations and isolated rutin papers include aging or lesion outcomes. Continue primary dyskinesia tests with toasted groats and quantify adverse outcomes.
Two cooked barley products had inconclusive dedicated anxiety contrasts or favorable within-arm subscales. The waxy barley cultivar trial did not measure anxiety separately.
